WHY: the story declares a story sub-kind `opening` (`is: [thing]`, `fixed: true`) on five fixed openings: back_door, house_gate, facility_gate, service_gate, storm_drain. A narration check measured on those things is about to be wired into the shared engine, scoped by that kind. The shared engine must not depend on one story's vocabulary, so `opening` becomes an engine base kind next to container, supporter, furniture and vehicle, that any story can use for doors, gates, hatches, drains and similar fixed openings that declare no open/closed state and no contents.

CHANGES:
1. worldkeeper: add `"opening": ("thing",)` to `BASE_KINDS` in packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py, and make an `opening` fixed by default (an entity of kind opening, or of a story kind descending from it, with no explicit `fixed`, is fixed; an explicit `fixed: false` still wins), the same way `furniture` is fixed by default today (see the `fixed = "furniture" in _ancestors(kinds, kind)` fallback). Nothing else changes in worldkeeper. Add worldkeeper tests: a story with no `kinds:` block can declare kind `opening`; it is a thing; it is fixed by default; explicit `fixed: false` wins; a story kind `is: [opening]` inherits fixed; a story trying to redeclare a kind named `opening` is rejected like any duplicate base kind.
2. world.yaml: delete the story kind entry `- id: opening` / `is: [thing]` / `fixed: true` from `kinds:` (it would now be a duplicate of the base kind). Keep `kind: opening` and `fixed: true` on the five items, and change nothing else in the file.
3. docs/world-model-grounding.md: in the 'Pick the kind that fits' bullet, add `opening` to the list of kinds and one plain sentence (12th-grade level, one idea per sentence) saying it is for a fixed door, gate, hatch or drain that declares no open or closed state and no contents, and that narration may not invent one. Update the 'Mark fixed: true' bullet only if needed to stay consistent (an opening is fixed by default). Keep the guide short.
4. Goldens: the world schema data changes (the kinds list no longer carries a story `opening` entry), so update EXPECTED_SCHEMA_HASH in tests/test_package_view_scope.py to the new value, after confirming with a before/after diff of `world_source_schema_data(package.world)` that the only change is that kinds entry. Keep tests/test_world_model.py's kind set correct (entity kinds still include `opening`). tests/test_world_placements.py's helper keeps story kinds; adjust only if the change requires it.

CONTEXT: `opening` is now an engine base kind (a fixed door, gate, hatch or drain with no declared open/closed state and no contents). An experiment (.plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration/t9h-opening-condition-v2-prereg.md and section 12 of .plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration/t9h-drain-condition-experiment-design.md) showed that one Jev question, "Variant B", separates narrations that invent an open/ajar/entered state or contents for such a thing from clean ones (drain 52/54 and 46/46; four other openings 19/19 and 21/21). The question and its state are in scripts/ringer/environment_narration/drain_condition_judge_probe.py: `_variant_b_question()` and `variant_b_payload(case)`, whose state is exactly {"narration", "thing", "command", "declared"} with declared = "the <thing name> has no open or closed value, no declared contents, and is fixed in place." It must be sent EXACTLY as measured: same question text, same state keys, its own Jev request (do not merge it into the observation-relation request, whose state differs).

BUILD, behind a flag that is OFF by default (with it off, behaviour, requests and prompts are byte-identical to today):
1. storygame/runtime/opening_check.py: the Variant B question as a runtime constant (copied text), a function that builds the state for one thing (narration, thing name, the player's command, the declared sentence), and the scoring/verdict using the same thresholds as ObservationVerifier (accept above .65, reject below .35, otherwise uncertain). Story-agnostic: it knows the kind name `opening` (an engine base kind) and nothing about any story.
2. Which things: the things the PLAYER'S COMMAND refers to this turn (the referent match's resolved refers for the turn) whose declared kind is or descends from `opening` (WorldSchema.kind_is). Find where capture/item_facts hold the turn's resolved referents and expose them to the verifier call without re-parsing anything. No command referent of kind opening means no opening request.
3. storygame/runtime/observation_verifier.py: `ObservationVerifier(..., opening_check=False)`. When on and the turn has opening subjects, `verify(...)` also asks one Jev request per opening subject (at most 2 opening requests per narration attempt; a separate per-turn budget from the relation requests, reset in begin_turn) and records the verdicts in the VerifierReport (new fields, defaults keeping old reports identical). `accepted` then also requires every opening verdict to be "accept" (fail closed exactly like the relation verdicts: reject, uncertain or unavailable are not accepted). When the turn has opening subjects but no required relations, the check must still run (today verify returns early with no_relations: keep that outcome when there are no opening subjects either). Run the opening request(s) concurrently with the relation request when both happen, using the existing ConcurrentCall in storygame/runtime/jev_prefetch.py; the background call must only do the Jev request and touch no world or provider state.
4. storygame/runtime/capture.py: pass the opening subjects and the command at both verify call sites (enforcing and shadow), and make sure the enforcing path actually calls verify when there are opening subjects even if there are no relations. A rejected opening verdict goes down the same retry/reject path as a rejected relation (do not invent a new path). Record the opening verdicts wherever relation verdicts are recorded for the bench rows (find where report fields are written).
5. storygame/web_demo.py: env flag `FREYTAG_OPENING_CHECK=1` turns `opening_check=True` on for the verifiers it builds, next to FREYTAG_OBSERVATION_SCENE_STATE. Default off.
6. docs/contributor-guide.md: if it counts Jev/verifier requests per turn, add one sentence that an opening check is one more Jev request per opening the command refers to (at most 2 per attempt), only with the flag on. Keep it short.
TESTS in tests/test_opening_check.py (hermetic, stub `ask`): the runtime question equals `_variant_b_question()` from the probe byte for byte (import it via importlib from the script path) and the state equals `variant_b_payload` for the same case; flag off sends no opening request and reports are identical to before; `Inspect the storm drain.`-style turn on the real package (scene 1B, the drain referred) sends one opening request with the drain's name and declared sentence; a turn referring to a container (the drawer) or a plain thing sends none; a rejected or uncertain opening verdict makes `accepted` false and an accepted one keeps it true; the opening request runs even with no required relations; the per-attempt budget caps opening requests at 2; the background call touches no FactStore (prove with a stub that fails if the FactStore is read off the main thread, or equivalent); the shadow and enforcing paths both pass the subjects. Keep all existing tests green.

HOW TO VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH: run `bash /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/check_t9h_opening_wiring.sh wiring`. Finish with a summary: the call flow (where subjects come from, where verify is called, how the verdict reaches the retry path), the exact flag, and the bench-row fields added.
